units: pixels and seconds; no metric scale inferred

camera.motion: static (phase-correlation shift 0.00 px for every frame vs frame 0)
camera.view: top-down (bird's-eye) onto rocky/mossy ground; 2D: butterfly flies in a plane parallel to the image
camera.perspective: none usable; ground fills the frame, no horizon

objects.name: butterfly
objects.description: single light-blue butterfly (morpho-like), seen from above, body axis horizontal, head to the LEFT (larger forewings on the left), wings spread up/down in the image
objects.reference_point: ref_x/ref_y = centre of the wing-mask bounding box; lies on the body at the forewing/hindwing junction (thorax); proxy for the rig origin (x stable under flapping because wings rotate about the horizontal body axis)

body_axis_length_px_horizontal_extent.note: horizontal (flight-direction) extent of the wings, not the body alone; 188-194 with wings open, 169-206 when folded

objects.body_alone: not measured: the thin dark body between the wings is barely distinguishable from the ground

objects.name: ground
objects.description: static rocky ground with stones, moss and grass patches covering the whole frame; no distinct markings

events.event: frames 0 and 1 identical (no motion between them)
wings edge-on (min apparent wingspan, wing beat)
steady flight leftwards, slight downward drift (~13 px over 70 frames); no stops or reversals; still in motion at last frame
